summary.headline: Bluspring FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 3,304 crore and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 4.2%, with STEAG and LSG acquisitions set to push margins toward 5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 8% YoY to INR 846 crore (flat QoQ) and EBITDA rose 44% YoY to INR 35 crore, with margin up 35 bps QoQ to 4.2%. Adjusted PAT (excluding the Q3 Labour Code one-off) grew 26-27% to INR 67 crore for FY26, and the company reported a net cash position of INR 15 crore at March 2026. Management signed definitive agreements to acquire STEAG Energy Services (India) and LSG Sky Chefs' Bengaluru operations, and guided to 15-16% organic growth in FY27. foundit showed its highest quarterly sales in six quarters (INR 26 crore) and narrowed EBITDA losses to INR 9 crore from INR 12 crore in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: +26-27% YoY, excludes Q3 Labour Code one-off

segments.name: Facility and Food Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,031 crore (+12% YoY); Q4 INR 519 crore (+10% YoY, flat QoQ). Q4 EBITDA INR 24 crore (+56% YoY), driven mainly by collections rather than volume; 24 new contracts with INR 124 crore ACV added.

segments.name: Telecom and Industrials
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 615 crore (+7% YoY) with telecom muted by delayed telecom capex; industrial sub-vertical grew 7% QoQ. Q4 revenue INR 157 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR 18 crore (+13% YoY, +19% QoQ); FY26 EBITDA INR 57 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Security Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 659 crore (+14% YoY); Q4 INR 169 crore (+15% YoY, flat QoQ). Headcount crossed 24,000 after about 2,900 guard additions in FY26; FY26 EBITDA INR 19 crore (+23% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR 6 crore.

segments.name: foundit (investment, shown separately)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 19 crore and sales INR 26 crore (vs average INR 17 crore in Q1-Q3 FY26). EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 9 crore in Q4 from INR 12 crore in Q3; management targets EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guided at 15-16%, with organic EBITDA margin around 4%; Q1 is seasonally soft in food and telecom, so margin may dip below 4% before recovering from Q2.
STEAG (about INR 700 crore revenue, high-single-digit EBITDA margin, expected INR 60-65 crore EBITDA) to be consolidated from around end-May 2026; management says closing is expected within the week.
LSG Bengaluru (about INR 110 crore revenue, 17-18% operating margin, about INR 20 crore EBITDA) expected to close in 30-60 days from the call; consolidation for 8-9 months in FY27.

Combined acquisitions expected to add about INR 800 crore annualised revenue and about INR 80 crore EBITDA, taking EBITDA margin toward 5%; management expects PAT above INR 100 crore annualised, excluding foundit.

foundit targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (Q4); management says the cost base supports breakeven at INR 34-35 crore revenue run rate, and it will consider monetising part of the stake.
Operating cash flow guided at 55-60% of operating EBITDA. Acquisition debt to be repaid aggressively after integration; funding via debt and internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Management says both acquired businesses are capex-light and does not foresee a large depreciation impact.
STEAG manages about 7 GW of power assets and 2,200 tph of process steam capacity, with over 2,000 employees.
LSG India Bengaluru holds in-flight catering facilities at Bengaluru airport under a concession running to 2039.
Bluspring workforce is above 93,000, up 6,600 during FY26.
demand_pricing: Q4 saw about 42 new contracts with ACV of INR 181 crore; FY26 total was 164 contracts with ACV of INR 459 crore.
Top 30 clients contribute less than 50% of revenue.
Margin gains attributed to new contracts at better margins, better collections and exiting low-margin clients; management says no further low-margin contracts remain to be exited.
Telecom revenue held back by delayed capex from leading telecom operators; industrial metals business gained new contracts at better margins.
Management says bankers and advisers, including big four diligence, drove the Q4 acquisition-related exceptional cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach a sustained 5% after STEAG consolidation, and when will both deals close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal estimates put margin in touching distance of 5%. STEAG was expected to close within the week, with consolidation from Q1; LSG was expected in 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% organic growth realistic given FY26 ACV of about INR 450 crore and contract losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was about 15-16% in FY26 before lost contracts, some lost to competition and some exited for low margins. It said no further deliberate exits are planned and the sales team is now fully built, supporting 15-16% guidance for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan and funding guardrail for foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term goal is EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; parent funds the shortfall within visible limits. Management will consider monetising part of the stake, and in the medium term may become a minority investor, once breakeven is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is STEAG's valuation (INR 180 crore EV, about INR 140 crore cash) sustainable given INR 65 crore EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said STEAG grew from INR 530 crore in FY24 to INR 600 crore in FY25 and INR 700 crore in FY26, with 3-5 year contracts giving about three years of visibility. The seller, a German group, is exiting India to focus on Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-Ind AS impact on EBITDA and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR 10 crore of the INR 121 crore EBITDA is from Ind AS. The only PAT adjustments are the INR 29 crore Labour Code one-off in Q3 and the INR 6.8 crore acquisition cost in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will foundit reach EBITDA neutral and PAT positive, and is the INR 100 crore PAT target ex-foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR 100 crore PAT target excludes foundit and that breakeven is expected by Q4 FY27. It said PAT-positive operation for foundit would need a run rate of about INR 34-35 crore, with no further people or product investment needed.

risks_watch: Acquisition integration of STEAG and LSG, and delivery of the stated synergies and cross-sell.
Acquisition-related debt repayment pace and funding mix (debt plus internal accruals).
Telecom segment recovery depends on the timing of telecom operators' capex.
foundit: quarter-one seasonality, AI-disruption risk to the talent platform, ongoing parent funding and the monetisation route.
Q1 FY27 margin seasonality in food and telecom may pull margin below 4%.
Management says organic FY27 revenue growth of 15-16% exceeds FY26 ACV-implied growth (about 10-13%), so the target needs to be tested.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, acquisitions and the FY27 organic outlook, and specific on numeric targets. Where questioned on foundit's losses and funding, answers were more hedged, with heavy reliance on timelines and the Q4 sales uptick rather than hard commitments.
key_quotes: And with these acquisitions, our internal estimate is that we should definitely be in the touching distance of 5% margins.
So, internally we've weeded out all those contracts, so we do not believe that the reduction should be of the magnitude that we saw in the year one.
So we are on that trajectory of an internally aligned of taking the company to a EBITDA break-even company by the end of this financial year.

adds.what: STEAG Energy Services acquisition (about 7 GW power assets, 2,200 tph process steam capacity); consolidated from around end-May 2026
LSG Sky Chefs Bengaluru in-flight catering facilities (concession to 2039); expected to close in 30-60 days

growth.why: Management guides 15-16% organic FY27 revenue growth and ~4% organic EBITDA margin, backed partly by 24 new contracts (INR 124 cr ACV) in Q4 and 42 contracts (INR 181 cr ACV), plus acquisitions of STEAG (~INR 700 cr revenue) and LSG Bengaluru (~INR 110 cr) adding ~INR 800 cr annualised revenue; organic capacity additions are not quantified.
